question: Who among the following was the first Indian musician to receive the Grammy Life Time Achievement Award?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Ravi Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar**, who was the** first Indian musician** to receive the Grammy Life Time Achievement Award in 2013.
 
• Pandit Ravi Shankar was a renowned Indian sitar player and composer who introduced Indian classical music to the Western world. He collaborated with several Western musicians, including George Harrison of The Beatles, and was awarded India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999.
 
• Nucleya is a popular Indian electronic music producer and DJ, known for his fusion of Indian folk and classical music with bass-heavy electronic beats. He has won several awards, including the MTV Europe Music Award for Best India Act in 2016.
 
• Hariprasad Chaurasia is a legendary Indian classical flautist, known for his mastery of the bansuri (bamboo flute). He has received several awards, including the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan, two of India's highest civilian honours.
 
• Ustad Zakir Hussain is a world-renowned Indian tabla player, known for his virtuosity and versatility. He has collaborated with several Western musicians, including John McLaughlin and Mickey Hart, and has won several awards, including the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Recording Academy bestows a unique Grammy Award known as the **Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award** on "performers who, during their lifetimes, have made creative contributions of outstanding artistic significance to the field of recording."
 
• This award is different from the Grammy Trustees Award, which celebrates non-performers, and the Grammy Hall of Fame Award, which honors certain records rather than individuals.
 
• The first recipient of the **accolade **was chosen in 1963, after it was created in 1962.
